description: Generate configuration variables and validators following naming conventions. Enforces typed, documented, validated environment variables at creation time.
context: Use when adding any new environment variable or configuration setting
checklist: 1. IDENTIFY MODULE AND RESOURCE: Determine the module (AUTH, DATABASE, PAYMENT, EMAIL, etc.) and resource (DATABASE, STRIPE, SENDGRID, etc.). Refer to .ai/config-vars.md for registry.
2. CHOOSE VARIABLE NAME: Follow {MODULE}_{RESOURCE}_{PROPERTY} pattern. Example: STRIPE_API_KEY, DATABASE_POOL_SIZE, JWT_SECRET
3. SELECT TYPE: Choose from: string, number, boolean, enum, secret, url, integer. Type determines validation rules.
4. DETERMINE REQUIRED: Mark as required (✅) if deployment fails without it, optional (—) if it has sensible default.
5. SET DEFAULT VALUE: Provide default for optional variables. Secrets should never have defaults.
6. CHECK FOR DUPLICATES: Verify variable name doesn't already exist. Command: python config/config_generator.py --check-exists STRIPE_API_KEY
7. CREATE VALIDATOR: Generate validation function (pydantic model, zod schema, joi schema) with type constraints.
8. UPDATE .env.example: Add variable with description and placeholder to .env.example (committed to git).
9. ADD TO REGISTRY: Register variable in .ai/config-vars.md or module's .ai/config-vars.md with type, required, default, purpose.
10. TEST VALIDATION: Verify validator accepts valid values and rejects invalid values.
11. SCAN FOR USAGE: Run config_discovery.py to find all places config is used and verify all match registry.
12. VALIDATE CONSISTENCY: Run config_validator.py to check all config at startup, no undeclared variables, secrets not logged.
13. REPORT SUCCESS: Confirm variable generated, type validated, .env.example updated, discovery passed
configuration: secret_safety: Never log, never default, always validate
